summary.headline: PSP Projects Q1 FY27 revenue rose 65% YoY to INR853 crores, with order book at INR13,245 crores (up 103% YoY) and EBITDA margin of 6.42%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 65% YoY to INR853 crores and EBITDA rose 121% to INR55 crores, with margin expanding to 6.42% from 4.79%. Net profit reached INR18 crores versus INR37 lakhs a year earlier. Management attributed the margin shortfall versus its 7-8% target to weak April-May billing against labour-heavy costs, with employee cost at 5.4% of sales. Management reiterated FY27 revenue of INR4,400-4,500 crores and a 7-8% EBITDA margin for the full year, with the bulk of improvement expected in the second half.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR35 crores; ~5.39% of sales; headcount ~2,400 to ~2,600

segments.name: Adani Group projects
segments.commentary: Management estimated roughly 45% of Q1 revenue came from Adani Group projects, including RVNL and SMC. Within the order book, group projects are about 70% (61% of the INR6,200 crore bid pipeline).

segments.name: Order book by sector
segments.commentary: Industrial 39%, residential 37%, government 23%, institutional about 1%. Q1 order inflow was INR630 crores, 93% from Adani Group.

segments.name: Precast
segments.commentary: No separate revenue disclosed. Management indicated plant capacity of about INR200 crores, with INR150-200 crores executed per year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue of INR4,400-4,500 crores reaffirmed; management expects average growth of more than 25% going forward.
EBITDA margin of 7-8% for the full year; management said the bulk of the improvement comes in the second half, and could go beyond 7-8% as execution speeds up.
Employee cost expected to normalise to 4-4.5% of sales once sales pick up and labour availability improves.
Capex guided at 3-4% of revenue; larger projects could push it higher.
Order inflow of INR400-500 crores above prior expectations is not assumed; management expects FY27 inflows in the INR4,000-5,000 crore range, with more projects expected to click in Q2 and Q3.
Management expects finance costs to fall further and says the company could become net debt-free within two to three quarters.
Guidance is on a consolidated basis, and government orders are excluded from inflow guidance until they are firm.
Expects end-FY27 order book of about INR1,000 crores above the INR5,000-6,000 crore range if more than INR4,000 crores is executed.
capex_capacity: Q1 capex of INR28 crores; guided to 3-4% of revenue on average.

Workforce of 16,000+ labourers deployed in Q1; management expects requirement of 16,000-17,000 at peak, with a further 3,000-4,000 to be added over the next one to two quarters as finishing and MEP work starts.
Mahim project: first two blocks raft foundation complete, now in first basement work. Matunga: piling under way, sheet piling before excavation.
SMC high-rise: core and shell complete, MEP, interiors and facade under way; completion expected by June 2027.
RVNL: two of three buildings to be handed over soon, hospital building RCC complete; project expected to complete by October 2026.
Ahmedabad Airport cityside: RCC work in full swing. Ambaji Mata Temple: excavation stage, some buildings at footing level.
demand_pricing: Order book INR13,245 crores as of 30 June 2026. Largest projects: Shree Ambaji Mata Temple INR962 crores, SMC High-Rise INR693 crores, GIFT City FinTech building INR259 crores, Science City gallery INR248 crores.
Bid pipeline of INR6,200+ crores, 61% group and 39% external.

Dharavi: about INR3,000 crores of the order book across two projects, which management equated to roughly 30,000-32,000 of the 2 lakh houses planned. Right of first refusal on further Dharavi work depends on performance over the next 1-2 years.

Cost escalation: aluminium and copper price increases hit some SMC and RVNL activities. Adani projects are pass-through, so management sees little impact there. Cost-plus contracts target about 7% EBITDA; Adani projects 6-7%, non-Adani 8-9%.

Management said the company will concentrate on Gujarat and Mumbai and aims for a 70-75% Adani / 25% non-Adani mix. Government order inflows are excluded until firm, and the Commonwealth Games project tender has not yet been issued.
UP medical project receivables: about INR40 crores receivable and INR60 crores unbilled; management expects EOTs to be signed and collections to close by end-August or mid-September 2026.
SDB receivables outstanding: INR90 crores; management plans a meeting with the counterparty's board.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR4,500 crore FY27 revenue target and 20-25% growth still intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reaffirmed INR4,400-4,500 crores and said average growth would exceed 25%.

qa_highlights.question: When does the 7%+ margin start, Q2 or H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 7%+ range comes from H2. Q1 margin was hit by about 1% from low April-May billing against labour cost. Q1 billing was INR319 crores in June versus INR270 crores in each of April and May.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company be net debt-free within two to three quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said this could happen as working capital use falls and surplus FDs build.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a Dharavi opportunity beyond the current two projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it holds the first right of refusal. Further projects depend on performance on the current two. Redevelopment of about 2 lakh houses over roughly five to six years is planned, with separate development of cleared land after that.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tax rate outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 tax rate was 35%. Management expects the full-year rate to be slightly above 25% because some expenses are non-deductible.

qa_highlights.question: Is the margin on cost-plus projects tightly controlled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cost-plus contracts work out to about 7% EBITDA, with a 1-2% gap depending on location (Mumbai about 3%, Mundra about 1.5%).

risks_watch: Margin delivery: Q1 EBITDA margin 6.42% vs 7-8% FY27 target; management says the bulk of improvement is in H2 and depends on April-May billing catching up, labour availability and employee cost falling to 4-4.5% of sales.

Receivables and collections: UP medical project (about INR40 crores receivable, INR60 crores unbilled) expected to close by end-August or mid-September 2026 once EOTs are signed; SDB receivables of INR90 crores still unresolved with a board meeting pending.
Order inflow visibility: Q1 inflow of INR630 crores (93% Adani); FY27 inflow guided at INR4,000-5,000 crores with government orders excluded until firm; Commonwealth Games tender not yet issued.
Adani concentration: about 45% of Q1 revenue and about 70% of order book from Adani Group; target mix of 70-75% Adani / 25% non-Adani.
Cost escalation: aluminium and copper price increases affected some SMC and RVNL activities; Adani projects are pass-through, but non-pass-through exposure on remaining projects is not quantified.
Dharavi: about INR3,000 crores of order book across two projects; right of first refusal on further work depends on performance over the next 1-2 years.
Working capital and tax: mobilisation advance of INR836 crores and trade receivables of INR745 crores; Q1 tax rate 35%, full-year rate guided slightly above 25% due to non-deductible expenses.
key_quotes: Yes, we can say it will be, on average, more than 25%. So, can be between INR4,400 to INR4,500. Still, we remain in the same line.
So, if you add at least that INR7 -INR 8 crores in the EBITDA, it will be somewhere above 7%. But okay, fine, but we will be in a better position in from Quarter 3 and Quarter 4.
No, no, it should be for the entire year, but once the execution speed is coming up in the next few quarters, we should be in a better position to go beyond 7% to 8%.
I don't have the exact figure what is coming from Dharavi side, but I think there are two projects of Dharavi which is considered in this order book.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the order book, revenue guidance (INR4,400-4,500 crores) and the H2 margin ramp, but noticeably cautious on Q1 margin, citing April-May labour shortages and low billing. Management was evasive on Commonwealth Games timing, the SDB receivable and the Dharavi share of future work, answering these with "not clear" or "difficult to say".
